highlights.title: Musk Says He’ll Gift SpaceX Shares to ‘Every Kid in America’
highlights.description: Elon Musk pledged to distribute a share of SpaceX to each American child, posting the move just hours after artificial intelligence competitor Anthropic PBC said it would set aside a portion of its shares for the public benefit.

alsoIn.title: Musk Pledges SpaceX Shares to ‘Every Kid in America’
Musk pledges to give ‘every kid in America’ one of his SpaceX shares

highlights.title: Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests
highlights.description: Arm claims its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the modeled rack performance of AMD’s EPYC 9755 across seven agentic AI workloads, using a new evaluation methodology developed with Fujitsu, Meta, and OpenAI

highlights.title: Samsung, SK Hynix Slide Causes $137 Billion Hit to Korea Pension
highlights.description: South Korea’s main pension fund took a 182 trillion won ($137 billion) hit after a decline in stakes of equities including Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc.

highlights.title: US Moves to Bar DeepSeek From Federal Agencies and Contracts
highlights.description: The Trump administration barred civilian US government agencies from using products or services from Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek, whose more affordable open-weight models pose an increasing challenge to Silicon Valley Valley developers.

highlights.title: Nscale Faces Pushback on $30 Billion IPO Valuation
highlights.description: Nscale, the data center developer backed by Nvidia, is facing opposition to the valuation target of about $30 billion that it’s pursuing in its IPO, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Ruhell Amin reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Elon Musk says he'll give a SpaceX share to every child in America next year
highlights.description: The SpaceX boss said Monday that he'll give one of his company shares to every child in the U.S. next year. He didn't say how the share giveaway would happen.

highlights.title: Google Gemini 4 agents just beat Minecraft with no human intervention
highlights.description: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft's Ender Dragon with no human intervention by sharing tips, threats and mistakes.

highlights.title: Google says it can build data centers the right way. Some experts and residents are skeptical
highlights.description: Google says its Minnesota AI data center will add clean energy to the grid and protect ratepayers. Experts question whether grid upgrades are needed.

highlights.title: US Futures Climb as Chips Rebound After Rout; CoreWeave Jumps
highlights.description: US stock futures are rebounding from the worst week for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index since the tariff turmoil of April 2025, as chips stocks and troubled artificial-intelligence bellwether CoreWeave Inc. rise ahead of the bell.

highlights.title: Uber Wins Bid to Dismiss £250 Million Black Cab Driver Suit
highlights.description: Uber Technologies Inc. won a bid to dismiss a £250 million ($333 million) lawsuit after a judge ruled that the claim on behalf of thousands of London’s black cab drivers was filed too late.

ev_autonomous.title: Boot this: BYD Denza B8 driver gets booted, doesn’t care [video]
ev_autonomous.description: The plug-in hybrid BYD Denza B8 didn’t set the sales charts on fire, but its high-tech suspension promised a smooth ride across just about any terrain, adjusting damping and ride height while independently controlling hydraulic pressure at each wheel. It’s a neat trick, but one driver has figured out a whole new use for it: avoiding traffic boots. more…

devices.title: Nobody should buy the $299 Apple TV 4K, but it could have been worse
devices.description: My colleague Zac Hall described HomeView as one of the best ways to spend $299 on an Apple device and the Apple TV 4K as the worst. Almost nobody thinks anyone should buy the latter at that price, but things could have been even worse … more…

devices.title: Constrained iPhone Duo availability is annoying, but a mixed blessing for Apple
devices.description: Estimated iPhone Duo delivery dates started slipping dramatically, literally within a minute of pre-orders opening on Friday. Even some of those who got in within the first few minutes got estimated shipping dates into January of next year. That undeniably poses problems for Apple, but some have gone as far as calling it “a major mistake” to launch with such limited stock. Personally, I’d say it’s annoying for customers but more of a mixed blessing for Apple … more…
